review.assessment: Scope is limited to the legacy Store::put_usage integer boundary. The guard is correct. `i64::try_from(u64)` accepts exactly 0..=i64::MAX, with no cast, clamp or zero substitution. It covers all six Option<u64> integer fields of domain::Usage; review_round is u32 and estimated_cost is f64 with its existing finiteness check. It runs after validate_scope and before the Session lookup and the Immediate transaction, so a rejection cannot leave Usage, audit or snapshot writes behind. Rejecting the whole legacy row instead of invalidating a single field departs from the qualified design ('Overflow invalidates the affected metric'). That is acceptable here: legacy rows stay unqualified and there is no production caller of put_usage. Per-field qualified invalidation stays an open design obligation, not a regression. The test round-trips i64::MAX through the real Session/Task fixture and rejects i64::MAX+1 and u64::MAX for each field independently while the other fields are valid. Its message check and full state-equality check are sound. The six public patches carry index 0a023c0, which matches the post-delta blob, and their hunk line numbers (832–843) match the guard's position, so each patch omits exactly one field. Each such mutant necessarily fails at its field-named expect_err. The 14 state tests counted in the ledger match the file. The doc delta keeps the qualified telemetry architecture explicitly unimplemented, makes no whole-#21 or native benchmark claim, and sets whole_issue_acceptance:false. Limitation: my attempted local git cross-checks (tree equality of the restore head, source_sha256 recomputation, caller grep) did not complete in this session. This review rests on the supplied public bytes and static reasoning. The CI, full-suite, fmt/clippy and build results are taken as reported, not re-verified. No Critical, High or Medium causal defects were found.

findings.claim: The ledger says the guard covers 'token counts', but one token counter persisted through put_usage stays unguarded. The sentence also credits the source change to the wrong commit.
findings.evidence: GrokAdapter::usage writes cache_metadata {"cache_creation_tokens": usage["cacheCreationTokens"].as_u64()}. That native token count can exceed i64::MAX. It is stored verbatim, because the new guard checks only the six typed fields and cache_metadata is arbitrary JSON. Separately, the guard itself was introduced in 5a2f47a. b47b773 only corrected the test fixture, yet the text reads 'Source b47b773 adds'.
findings.fix: Wording only; do not add a cache_metadata validator in this component. State that the guard covers exactly the six typed Usage integer fields. List integers inside arbitrary cache_metadata (including Grok cache_creation_tokens) as an explicit unguarded, unqualified exclusion until raw-writer retirement. Say the guard landed in 5a2f47a and was validated at b47b773.

review.assessment:
No Critical, High or Medium causal defect was found in this narrow component.

Guard behaviour (crates/rrx/src/state/mod.rs put_usage):
- i64::try_from(u64) accepts exactly 0..=i64::MAX. flatten() skips None, so a missing value stays missing and is never turned into zero.
- Nothing is cast, clamped or relabelled; the stored body is the caller's original Usage.
- The ensure! runs after validate_scope and before the Session lookup and the Immediate transaction. A rejection therefore cannot append a Usage row or a usage.recorded audit event, and cannot touch Project, Goal, Task or Session.
- Existing cost, missing-reason, Session-scope and agent checks are unchanged.
- Callers are unaffected in practice. Generic input_bytes comes from a payload length and always fits. Generic context_pack_version comes from a u64 input version, so a value above i64::MAX is now deliberately refused at put_usage; there is still no production caller of put_usage. The Generic Store-persistence test and the existing state tests use small values.

Test (usage_integer_overflow_cannot_publish_rows_or_audit_or_change_owners):
- It uses a genuine put_task/put_session fixture inside Project.worktree_root.
- It persists i64::MAX on five fields and zero on one, and asserts exact readback.
- It drives each field independently to both i64::MAX+1 and u64::MAX while the other fields stay valid.
- It requires the specific 'supported storage range' message, so a refusal for an unrelated reason earns no credit.
- It compares the serialized Project, Goal, Task, Session, usage rows and task-scoped audit before and after each attempt.

Mutation evidence:
- All six public patches match the post-change blob 0a023c0 line for line (hunks at 832–837).
- Each patch compiles: it only shrinks an array literal.
- Without the guard, an overflow body would previously have been accepted: json_valid accepts large integers and serde round-trips u64. So each mutant's put_usage returns Ok and panics at its own field-named expect_err, which matches the recorded exit code 101.

Scope and claims:
- The design and verification text keep Req8/Design4 qualified telemetry, raw-writer retirement, producers, epoch, native benchmark and whole-#21 acceptance open.
- They make no clamp, missing-zero, qualification or native-default claim.
- The fixture-setup failures in 5a2f47a and c0267f4 are retained without credit.

This approval covers only the legacy integer storage boundary. It is not source, telemetry or benchmark acceptance for #21. The declared pending gates remain: exact-head Linux/macOS CI for this new source and the other independent source review.
